title: [MPS] Binary ops with a 0-dim CPU float tensor ignore storage_offset, silently using the wrong value
body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

On MPS, a binary op between an MPS tensor and a **0-dim CPU float tensor with a non-zero storage offset** silently uses the value at storage offset 0 instead of the actual value. No error, no warning — just a wrong number.

`coeffs[i]` for `i > 0` is exactly this kind of tensor, so any code that keeps a table of coefficients on the CPU and scales an MPS tensor by one of them gets silently wrong arithmetic.

```python
import torch

mps = torch.full((2, 2), 4.0, device="mps")
coeffs = torch.tensor([9.0, 2.0, 7.0])          # plain CPU tensor

for i in range(3):
    s = coeffs[i]                                # 0-dim CPU view, storage_offset == i
    got = (mps * s).flatten()[0].item()
    print(f"coeffs[{i}] = {float(s)}  offset={s.storage_offset()}  "
          f"mps * coeffs[{i}] -> {got}  expected {4.0 * float(s)}")
```

```
coeffs[0] = 9.0  offset=0  mps * coeffs[0] -> 36.0  expected 36.0
coeffs[1] = 2.0  offset=1  mps * coeffs[1] -> 36.0  expected 8.0     <-- wrong
coeffs[2] = 7.0  offset=2  mps * coeffs[2] -> 36.0  expected 28.0    <-- wrong
```

Every result uses `coeffs[0]`.

**Scope**, all measured on the same machine:

| case | result |
|---|---|
| 0-dim CPU, `storage_offset == 0` | correct |
| 0-dim CPU, `storage_offset != 0`, **float32 / float16** | **silently wrong** (reads offset 0) |
| 0-dim CPU, `storage_offset != 0`, int32 / int64 | correct |
| `coeffs[1].clone()` (offset reset to 0) | correct |
| 1-dim CPU tensor, e.g. `coeffs[1:2]` | correctly raises `RuntimeError: Expected all tensors to be on the same device` |

All binary ops are affected, in both operand orders:

```
mps * s  ->  36.000  expected  8.000
s * mps  ->  36.000  expected  8.000
mps / s  ->   0.444  expected  2.000
mps + s  ->  13.000  expected  6.000
mps - s  ->  -5.000  expected  2.000
```

So the 0-dim CPU-scalar promotion path appears to read the storage rather than the tensor's offset, and only for floating dtypes.

**Why it matters in practice.** I found this from the other end: two schedulers in `huggingface/diffusers` return all-NaN output on MPS while being correct on CPU. Both keep their `alphas`/`betas` coefficient tables on the CPU and do `sample * self.betas[i]`, so from step 1 onward they silently multiply by the wrong coefficient and diverge into NaN.

```python
# diffusers 0.40.0.dev0, same seed, same inputs
IPNDMScheduler           cpu: finite, mean -0.0586    mps: 4096/4096 NaN
KDPM2DiscreteScheduler   cpu: finite, mean -1.2485    mps: 4096/4096 NaN
```

The failure is silent end-to-end: a user on Apple Silicon gets a black image and no error. I plan to file the downstream issue on diffusers separately, since they can also defend against this by moving the coefficient tensors onto the sample's device — but the wrong arithmetic itself looks like it belongs here.

### Versions

```
PyTorch version: 2.13.0
Is debug build: False
OS: macOS-26.0.1-arm64-arm-64bit (Apple Silicon)
Python version: 3.11.14
MPS available: True
MPS built: True
```

2.13.0 is the current release, so this is not a stale-version report.

---

Disclosure, per [AI_POLICY.md](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/main/AI_POLICY.md): I used an AI coding assistant to help narrow this down, starting from the NaN outputs in diffusers and bisecting to the `storage_offset` condition. Every result above I ran myself on the machine described, and the reproduction is deliberately reduced to plain PyTorch with no third-party dependency so it can be checked in a few seconds. I have not looked at the MPS kernel source, so I have no proposed fix — the offset/dtype pattern is an observation from the outside.
provenance: Background issue: existed upstream before case 11 was opened. Created in the sandbox with the agent DISABLED and with the labels a maintainer had applied, so it is part of the repository state, not a test case.
